title: Quantum memory in an effective $Λ$-type system using dynamic detuning control of a superconducting qubit pair
authors: Hsin Chang, Kai-I Chu, Ite A. Yu, Yen-Hsiang Lin, Yung-Fu Chen
abstract: We theoretically investigate quantum-light storage in an effective $Λ$-type system formed by a pair of tunable superconducting qubits coupled to a semi-infinite transmission line and separated by half a wavelength. The frequency detuning between the qubits directly couples the superradiant excited state and the subradiant metastable state. By adjusting the qubit detuning, the system exhibits a controllable spectral response accompanied by slow-light behavior. Dynamically controlling the detuning enables an incident quantum field to be mapped onto the subradiant collective state, stored as a long-lived excitation, and subsequently retrieved on demand. Our results establish the proposed system as a minimal and tunable quantum-memory architecture for scalable superconducting quantum networks.
summary: This theoretical study proposes using a pair of superconducting qubits coupled to a transmission line to create a tunable quantum memory. By dynamically controlling the qubit detuning, the system can store an incoming quantum light pulse into a long-lived subradiant state. This establishes the system as a viable, minimal architecture for superconducting quantum networks.
main_problem: The paper investigates realizing quantum-light storage in a controllable, minimal, and tunable quantum memory architecture using superconducting qubits.
main_result: Dynamic control of the qubit detuning allows for the coherent mapping of an incident quantum field onto a long-lived subradiant collective state, enabling high-fidelity storage and on-demand retrieval.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling, solving the Lindblad master equation via the input-output formalism to simulate the system dynamics.
model_or_system: The system consists of a pair of tunable superconducting qubits coupled to a semi-infinite transmission line, forming an effective $\Lambda$-type system. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian and a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Reflection phase ($	heta_R$), group delay ($t_d$), quantum fidelity ($F_q$), storage efficiency ($\eta$), and photon flux ($n_L$).
important_parameters: The detuning ($\delta$) is the key control parameter, which is dynamically varied to achieve storage. Other parameters include coupling strengths ($\Omega_p$) and decay rates ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting qubit pure dephasing ($\Gamma_\phi = 0$) and using the collective-state basis transformation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the reflection phase ($	heta_R$) dependence on detunings, single-photon fluxes, and the calculated group delay time ($t_d$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the effective $\Lambda$-system, derives the Hamiltonian and master equation, and then uses the input-output formalism to demonstrate how time-dependent detuning control enables coherent quantum light storage and retrieval.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum networking by proposing a superconducting circuit platform that functions as a tunable quantum memory, which is a core component for quantum repeaters and quantum information processing.
